compass.name: Operation Compass
compass.strategic_context: British counteroffensive against Italian invasion of Egypt. Italy invaded Sept 1940, Britain counterattacked Dec 1940. Devastating British victory capturing 130,000 prisoners and destroying 10 Italian divisions. Germans NOT yet in North Africa.
compass.outcome: Decisive British victory, Italy requests German aid

sonnenblume.name: Operation Sonnenblume
sonnenblume.strategic_context: German deployment to North Africa following Italian collapse in Operation Compass. Rommel arrives Feb 12, 1941 with 5th Light Division. Immediately launches offensive, recapturing Cyrenaica and pushing British back to Egyptian frontier. Establishes siege of Tobruk (Apr 10).
sonnenblume.outcome: Axis success, British retreat to Egypt, Tobruk besieged
sonnenblume.notes: 15th Panzer Division arrives May-June 1941, NOT during Sonnenblume

tobruk.name: Siege of Tobruk
tobruk.strategic_context: Australian and British garrison holds Tobruk port under siege. Critical to deny Rommel the port and tie down Axis forces. Supplied by Royal Navy destroyers ('Tobruk Ferry Service'). Rommel launches multiple assaults, all repelled. Siege lifted during Operation Crusader (Nov-Dec 1941).

battleaxe.name: Operation Battleaxe
battleaxe.strategic_context: British offensive to relieve Tobruk garrison using 'Tiger Convoy' tank reinforcements (240 tanks). Failed due to German 88mm anti-tank screen at Halfaya Pass ('Hellfire Pass'). Demonstrated effectiveness of integrated German combined-arms tactics. Churchill's first major setback in desert.

crusader.name: Operation Crusader
crusader.strategic_context: Largest British offensive to date. Relieved Tobruk siege (242 days) and pushed Rommel back to El Agheila. Confused tank battles around Sidi Rezegh. Rommel's 'dash to the wire' failed. British logistical superiority prevailed despite tactical setbacks. Temporary British success.

gazala.name: Battle of Gazala
gazala.strategic_context: Rommel's greatest victory. Sweeping left hook around Gazala Line defensive boxes. 'Cauldron' battle where Rommel consolidated behind British lines. Free French heroic defense at Bir Hacheim. British armor defeated piecemeal. Tobruk falls (June 21) with 33,000 prisoners. Rommel promoted to Field Marshal. Advance to El Alamein.
gazala.outcome: Decisive Axis victory, advance to Egypt

first_alamein.name: First Battle of El Alamein
first_alamein.strategic_context: Critical defensive battle. Auchinleck halts Rommel just 60 miles from Alexandria. El Alamein position between sea and Qattara Depression prevents flanking. Series of attritional attacks exhaust both sides. High-water mark of Axis expansion. Rommel's logistics overstretched. British prevent breakthrough to Nile Delta.
first_alamein.outcome: British defensive victory, Axis advance halted

alam_halfa.name: Battle of Alam Halfa
alam_halfa.strategic_context: Montgomery's first battle as 8th Army commander. Rommel's final offensive attempt before British reinforcements arrive. British fight defensive battle from prepared positions on Alam Halfa ridge. RAF air superiority dominant. German fuel shortages critical. Rommel forced to retreat. Turning point - Axis never offensive again in North Africa.
alam_halfa.outcome: British defensive victory, Rommel's last offensive fails

second_alamein.name: Second Battle of El Alamein
second_alamein.strategic_context: Montgomery's set-piece breakthrough battle. Operation Lightfoot (infantry phase) followed by Supercharge (armor breakthrough). Overwhelming British material superiority (195,000 vs 104,000 men, 1,029 vs 547 tanks). Hitler's 'stand or die' order ignored. Rommel's long retreat begins. Churchill: 'This is not the end, not even the beginning of the end, but perhaps the end of the beginning.'
second_alamein.outcome: Decisive British victory, beginning of end for Axis in Africa

torch.name: Operation Torch
torch.strategic_context: Allied amphibious landings in Morocco and Algeria. American combat debut in North Africa. Vichy French resistance ends after 3 days. Opens second front, trapping Axis between Montgomery (east) and Eisenhower (west). Germans rush reinforcements to Tunisia. Race for Tunis begins. Strategic turning point - Axis now fighting defensive campaign on two fronts.
torch.notes: NOT in Egypt/Libya - this is Morocco/Algeria landings

tunisia.name: Tunisia Campaign
tunisia.strategic_context: Final campaign in North Africa. Axis trapped between two Allied armies. Kasserine Pass (Feb 1943) - American baptism of fire, tactical defeat but strategic lesson. Mareth Line breakthrough (Mar). Montgomery from east, Anderson/Patton from west. Axis supply cut by Malta-based air/naval forces. Von Arnim replaces Rommel (Mar). Final collapse May 1943 - 275,000 Axis prisoners.
tunisia.outcome: Allied victory, end of Axis in North Africa

mareth.name: Battle of Mareth Line
mareth.strategic_context: Breaking the last major Axis defensive line. Old French fortifications (Maginot-style). Montgomery's frontal assault (XXX Corps) stalls. Freyberg's New Zealand Corps 'left hook' via Tebaga Gap succeeds. Axis retreat to Wadi Akarit. Part of final Tunisia campaign. Rommel had already left Africa (Mar 9). Von Arnim in command.
mareth.outcome: British victory, breach of Mareth Line
mareth.notes: Rommel NOT present - left Africa March 9, 1943
